samples.summary: Overlay-guard is unrequested scope creep and changes ←/→ behavior the issue lists as "Unchanged"
samples.evidence: The task/issue plan (docs/tasks/active/20260822-image-viewer-back-button-todo.md:35) scopes image-viewer.tsx to "optional `onClose`; `Escape` calls it in the existing keydown handler (same input/contenteditable guard as ←/→)", and acceptance criterion at line 22 states "Unchanged: pdf/file layouts, ←/→ prev/next, zoom, download, share." The diff instead adds a whole `OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR`/`hasOpenOverlay()` mechanism (image-viewer.tsx:14-42) applied *before* the arrow-key branches (line 158), so ←/→ prev/next now silently stops working whenever any Radix dialog/menu/listbox/popper content is open, and moves the listener to window capture phase (line 163). That is a behavior change to a criterion declared unchanged, plus new mechanism not in the plan; if the double-Esc problem must be solved, the minimal fit is to guard Esc only, leaving ←/→ as-is.

samples.summary: Overlay detection is a hand-rolled coupling to Radix's internal markup, embedded in a leaf viewer instead of a shared primitive
samples.evidence: `OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR` hard-codes Radix internals (`data-radix-popper-content-wrapper`, `data-slot="tooltip-content"`, `data-state="open"`) inside image-viewer.tsx. No such helper exists elsewhere (only an ad-hoc popper-wrapper `closest()` in app/spreadsheet/components/comments/CommentPopover.tsx:61), so this is a new cross-cutting concern living at the wrong layer: if it is needed at all it belongs in a shared hook/util next to the ui/dialog+sidebar primitives (or should use Radix's own dismissable-layer/onEscapeKeyDown APIs) so the next global-key consumer does not re-derive the selector list.

samples.summary: New hook de-duplicates only the /f/:id copy of a slug-fallback that is repeated in five other detail pages
samples.evidence: The exact `workspaceSlug ?? workspaces[0]?.slug` → `/w/:slug` else `/documents` logic also exists in app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:76-81, app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:107-112, app/board/board-detail.tsx:51-56, app/documents/document-detail.tsx:189-194 and app/slides/slides-detail.tsx:114-119. Extracting it into `app/files/use-documents-path.ts` (a files-only location) leaves five other copies and makes future reuse awkward; a shared location (e.g. next to api/workspaces or a hooks module) would fit the repo's reuse expectation better. The task file's non-goals do not forbid this, so it is a taste/placement point rather than a spec breach.

samples.summary: FileShell now derives the same workspace twice — its own `currentWorkspace`/`workspaceSlug` plus `useDocumentsPath`
samples.evidence: Lines 58-62 keep the inline `workspaces.find(...)` slug derivation (used for nav items) while also calling `useDocumentsPath(documentData?.workspaceId)`, so the shell holds two derivations of the same fact with different fallback behavior (nav items get no first-workspace fallback, the redirect does). Passing the resolved base path (or having the hook also return the workspace) would leave one source of truth.

finding.summary: Overlay-guard is unrequested scope creep and changes ←/→ behavior the issue lists as "Unchanged"
finding.evidence: The task/issue plan (docs/tasks/active/20260822-image-viewer-back-button-todo.md:35) scopes image-viewer.tsx to "optional `onClose`; `Escape` calls it in the existing keydown handler (same input/contenteditable guard as ←/→)", and acceptance criterion at line 22 states "Unchanged: pdf/file layouts, ←/→ prev/next, zoom, download, share." The diff instead adds a whole `OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR`/`hasOpenOverlay()` mechanism (image-viewer.tsx:14-42) applied *before* the arrow-key branches (line 158), so ←/→ prev/next now silently stops working whenever any Radix dialog/menu/listbox/popper content is open, and moves the listener to window capture phase (line 163). That is a behavior change to a criterion declared unchanged, plus new mechanism not in the plan; if the double-Esc problem must be solved, the minimal fit is to guard Esc only, leaving ←/→ as-is.

verdict.reason: The code exists as quoted (OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR/hasOpenOverlay at image-viewer.tsx:14-42, applied before the arrow branches at :158, window capture listener at :163), but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) It does not fail the "Unchanged: ←/→ prev/next" criterion in substance: in the normal viewer state the arrow path is unchanged, and the guard only engages while a Radix layer with data-state="open" is above the viewer — a state where arrow-driven navigation behind an open modal was itself a defect and would also break the same criterion's "share" item; tooltips and non-open states are explicitly excluded (image-viewer.tsx:27-37) and tested (__tests__/image-viewer.test.tsx:131-139), so prev/next is never silently dead with nothing on screen. (b) The behavior is documented in the canonical subsystem design doc rather than a parallel file (docs/design/image-viewer.md:168-183), satisfying the design-doc discipline requirement. (c) The remaining objection — "guard Esc only, leave ←/→ as-is" — is a minimality/taste preference about a two-line condition inside the same handler the plan already required to change; the rubric classifies taste/"could be cleaner" as minor, which never blocks. No stated Non-Goal (todo.md:42-47) is exceeded, nothing is duplicated, and capture-phase key listeners are existing repo practice (components/toolbar-focus-release.ts:122).
